mainEntity.name: How much does a Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi (G3LA/G3LB) engine typically costs between £1,500 and £2,800 for supply only, depending on the exact code and generation.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi G3LA timing chain to fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: The G3LA 1.0 T-GDi timing chain fails due to restricted oil flow to the hydraulic tensioner, causing premature stretch and cold-start rattling.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, replacing the engine is worthwhile if the car is under 10 years old and the chassis is in good condition.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard supply and fit service for the Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi typically takes 2 to 3 days.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between G3LA and G3LB engines in the Kona 1.0 T-GDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The G3LA is the original 1.0 T-GDi engine fitted to 2017-2020 Kona models, while the G3LB is the updated Smartstream version fitted from 2021 onwards.

commonProblems.h2: Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi (G3LA/G3LB) is a popular choice for urban drivers, but the three-cylinder turbo architecture introduces specific wear points. Timing chain tensioner fatigue on early G3LA units and turbo wastegate issues on later G3LB models are the most prominent failure patterns. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded internal components designed to address these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi G3LA Rattles on Cold Starts
problems.rootCause: Restricted oil flow to the hydraulic tensioner due to narrow feed galleries and extended service intervals causes the timing chain to elongate, leading to misalignment and a distinct metallic rattle during cold ignition.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full chain, guides, tensioner and VVT actuator replacement with updated oil flush.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only before rattle becomes severe or cam phasing fails. Extends life 40k-60k miles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Bench-tested rebuilt unit with upgraded chain system, new seals, and reinforced tensioner.
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent resolution. Includes 12-month warranty and eliminates repeat timing chain failure risk.

problems.recommendation: On a Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi, timing chain stretch at low mileages is a known design weakness. If the engine is already rattling or throwing P0014 codes, internal wear on cam lobes and guides has likely occurred. We recommend a full Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi engine replacement in these cases, as a piecemeal chain kit rarely outlasts the weakened block components on high-mileage examples.

problems.group: Turbo Wastegate Rattle & GDI Carbon Buildup
problems.h4: Turbo Wastegate Rattle & GDI Carbon Buildup - Why the Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi Loses Boost
problems.rootCause: The turbo wastegate actuator can stick due to thermal cycling, causing boost irregularities and check engine lights. Concurrently, direct injection (GDI) prevents fuel from washing the intake valves, leading to severe carbon buildup that restricts airflow and causes rough idling.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Walnut blasting intake ports, replacing VVT solenoids, and turbo actuator calibration.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for mild rattling or rough idle, but does not fix worn turbo bearings.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement unit with upgraded oil pump, revised piston ring tension, and full supply & fit.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary when turbine fragments have entered the cylinders or carbon buildup has caused severe valve damage.

items.question: What causes the Hyundai Kona 1.0 T-GDi G3LA timing chain to fail?
items.answer: The G3LA 1.0 T-GDi timing chain fails due to restricted oil flow to the hydraulic tensioner, causing premature stretch and cold-start rattling.
keyPoints: Oil starvation from extended service intervals damages the hydraulic tensioner first.
Ignoring the rattle can lead to catastrophic valve-piston contact.
Upgraded tensioner kits exist, but full engine replacement is often safer for high-mileage units.
